# Facial Expression Recognition Based on TensorFlow

# Jiyang Gao

Chengdu College of University of Electronic Science and Technology of China，Chengdu，China

1749100495@qq.com

Abstract. Facial expression recognition is an important research direction in the field of computer vision, which has a wide range of application potential, including human-computer interaction, emotional computing, security monitoring, and so on. In this study, a facial expression recognition method based on the TensorFlow framework is proposed, which uses a convolutional neural network (CNN) to automatically extract facial features and classify emotions. By training with the FER2013 dataset, we construct a multi-layer convolutional neural network model and use data enhancement technology to improve the generalization ability of the model. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively identify seven basic emotions (happiness, sadness, anger, disgust, surprise, fear, and neutrality), and the classification accuracy on the FER2013 dataset reaches 70%, which is superior to other traditional facial expression recognition methods. Through the analysis of the confusion matrix and classification report, we find that the model is confused in some emotional categories (such as fear and sadness), and the accuracy and robustness can be further improved by optimizing the model structure or introducing stronger regularization methods in future work.

Keywords: facial expression recognition, convolutional neural network, TensorFlow, data enhancement, FER2013, emotion classification.

## 1. Introduction

Facial expression is an important expression of human emotions and intentions, which can convey rich social information. Whether in daily communication or on specific social occasions, facial expressions play a vital role. Static facial expression recognition has a wide application potential in psychology, sociology, and computer science, such as human-computer interaction, emotional calculation, and security monitoring. Through the analysis of facial expressions, we can better understand the individual emotional state, thus improving interpersonal communication and interaction between machines and people. With the rapid development of deep learning technology, especially convolutional neural networks (CNN[1]), the accuracy and efficiency of facial expression recognition have been significantly improved. CNN can automatically extract image features through multi-layer nonlinear transformation, which avoids the complexity and limitations brought by the manual design of features in traditional methods. This makes facial expression recognition not only more efficient but also more robust when dealing with complex scenes. In the framework of equal-depth learning such as TensorFlow[2], pre-training models (such as VGGFace[3] and ResNet[4]) can be used to conduct transfer learning. This method allows us to finetune the existing powerful model to meet the specific application requirements. In this way, we can not only reduce the training time but also significantly improve the performance of the model. These pre-training models have been trained on a large number of facial data, so they can effectively extract facial features and improve the accuracy of recognition. In recent years, several facial expression recognition datasets have appeared, such as FER2013[5], CK+[6], and AffectNet[7] and so on, which provide a rich sample base for model training. These datasets contain facial images of various emotional states, covering individuals of different ages, genders, and races, which enables the model to learn more universal features. In addition, by enhancing the dataset, such as rotation, scaling, and flipping, the generalization ability of the model can be effectively improved, and the recognition accuracy can be further improved.

Before the research, we studied the traditional facial expression classification method. Although the traditional method used deep learning to improve the recognition effect, it still faced the challenges of fitting and environmental factors. Although the deep learning method has improved recognition accuracy, its adaptability to different lighting conditions, facial angles, and expression changes is still insufficient. In order to solve these problems, the attention network method is proposed[8]. By focusing on key facial areas, the recognition accuracy can be improved. This method significantly improves the ability of micro-expression recognition by dynamically adjusting the attention of the network to different facial regions. However, as the complexity of the model increases, so does the demand for computing resources, which limits its feasibility in real-time applications. Then real-time recognition based on TensorFlow[9] and VGG16 migration learning [10] are proposed. The use of the framework TensorFlow[2] can significantly reduce the training time while maintaining high recognition accuracy. Especially in the scene of video stream processing, the demand for real-time identification is particularly urgent. However, the performance of these methods in different environments is still unsatisfactory, especially in complex backgrounds or dynamic scenes, and the recognition accuracy has declined. While VGG16 transfer learning[10] performs well under certain conditions, the demand for computing resources is high, which limits its application in resource-limited devices. Although transfer learning can effectively use the existing knowledge, in practical application, how to balance the complexity of the model and the demand for computing resources is still an important issue. Combined with the above research, in the study of facial expression classification based on TensorFlow[2], this study uses the convolutional neural network (CNN)[1]. CNN[1] can effectively capture local features in images by convolution layer. With the increase of network depth, CNN[1] can extract more complex features layer by layer, from simple edges to complex facial expressions. This process not only improves the efficiency of feature extraction but also enhances the model’s ability to recognize different expressions. Another reason to use TensorFlow[2] is its flexible API design, which can build and modify models according to requirements and adapt to different facial expression classification tasks. TensorFlow[2] can use the static Graph for optimization, which can improve computational efficiency and resource utilization. The activity of the community and rich document resources of TensorFlow[2] provide good support for the research, and can quickly get started and realize complex models. In terms of datasets, the appearance of FER2013[5], CK+[6], and AffectNet[7] provides a rich sample base for model training. These datasets contain a variety of facial expression labeling data, which can effectively support the training and verification of the model. By rotating, scaling, and flipping, the dataset is enhanced, and the generalization ability of the model is improved, so that the model can still maintain high recognition accuracy when dealing with unknown data.

This section focuses on the construction process of the facial expression recognition model. Facial expression recognition is an important task in the field of computer vision. It aims to identify and classify different emotional states by analyzing facial images. The whole process can be divided into five main steps: dataset preparation, data preprocessing, model construction, model training, and result evaluation. This project is based on the platform TensorFlow[2] for experiments. TensorFlow[2] is an opensource machine learning framework developed and maintained by Google. It provides a flexible ecosystem that supports the construction and training of simple models to complex deep-learning algorithms.

The dataset FER2013[5] was released in 2013, which is an important dataset widely used in facial expression recognition research. The image data of this dataset comes from social media and other public data sources, and the facial expression images of individuals of different ages, genders, and races are collected. The main features of the dataset are as follows: the dataset FER2013[5] contains about 35,887 facial images. The samples of the dataset come from individuals of different ages, covering all genders. The specific age and gender ratio information was not listed in detail at the time of publication, but the samples were diverse and reflected the emotional expression of different people. The dataset labels seven basic emotions, including happiness, sadness, anger, disgust, surprise, fear, and neutrality. All images are grayscale images with a size of 48x48 pixels, which are suitable for computer vision tasks.

### 3.2 Data processing

Data preprocessing is a key step to improve the image classification effect. In this experiment, the main goal of data preprocessing is to convert the original image into a format suitable for model training. Firstly, the dataset is read, and the data file in CSV format is read by Pandas library, and it is converted into DataFrame format for subsequent processing. Then, emotional tags are screened to ensure that the dataset only contains effective emotional tags (0 to 6) to avoid interference with model training. Then the pixel data of each image is converted into NumPy array format. The specific operation is to divide and reshape each pixel value string into a 48x48 two-dimensional array, and finally stack it into a three-dimensional array for input into the deep learning model. Then, the emotional tag is coded and converted into a single-hot coding format to meet the output requirements of the model. Finally, the pixel values are normalized to [0, 1] to improve the training effect of the model. This step is helpful to speed up the convergence of the model and reduce the numerical instability in the training process. First, images and emotional tags are loaded from the FER2013 dataset. This dataset contains images of various facial expressions and marks them as seven emotions: anger, disgust, fear, happiness, sadness, surprise, and neutrality. ### 3.3 Model structure

CNN[1] is an important model in deep learning and is widely used in image classification, object detection, and image segmentation. By increasing the depth of the network, DCNN[12] can extract complex features more effectively and improve the performance of the model. In this experiment, the model DCNN[12] consists of several convolution layers, a pooling layer, a batch normalization layer, a Dropout layer, and a fully connected layer. The convolution layer uses multiple convolution kernels to extract the features of the input image, and the activation function uses ELU to introduce nonlinearity. The pool layer reduces the size of the feature map through the largest pool layer, reduces the computational complexity, and retains important information. Then batch normalization is added after each convolution layer to improve the training speed and stability. This study uses Dropout before the fully connected layer to prevent the model from over-fitting. The extracted features are flattened and input to the fully connected layer for final classification, and the category probability is output. This study builds a DCNN[12] model and uses Sequential API to build network structure. The model includes several convolution layers, a pooling layer, a batch normalization layer, a full connection layer, and a Dropout layer to extract image features and classify emotions. This study uses cross-entropy loss function and Adam optimizer to compile the model. This study sets an appropriate learning rate to ensure that the model can converge effectively. ### 3.4 Experimental setting

The training process of the model is very important and directly affects the final recognition effect. The model is trained by Nadam optimizer, and the number of training rounds is set to 100 and the batch size is 32. EarlyStopping and ReduceLROnPlateau callback functions are used in the training process to prevent over-fitting and adjust the learning rate. This study evaluates the performance of the model on the test set and calculates the classification report, including accuracy, recall, and F1 score. The confusion matrix is used to visualize the classification results of the model to identify the performance of the model in different emotions. Among them, EarlyStopping is used to monitor the accuracy of the verification set. When the accuracy of the verification set has not improved in 11 consecutive rounds, the training will be stopped in advance and the optimal weight will be restored. ReduceLROnPlateau is used to monitor the accuracy of the validation set. When the accuracy does not improve within seven consecutive rounds, the learning rate is reduced by half, so that the model can be fine-tuned at a smaller learning rate.

## 4. Experimental Results

### 4.1 Analysis of model accuracy and loss value

The changing trend of the accuracy of the model on the training set and the verification set is shown in Figure 5. As can be seen from the figure, with the increase in training rounds, the accuracy of the training set and verification set is on the rise. In the initial stage (the first 10 rounds), the accuracy of the training set improved rapidly, while the accuracy of the verification set improved slowly, indicating that the model gradually learned effective features from the training data in the early stage. In the middle and late stages of training, the accuracy of the verification set gradually approaches that of the training set, and both of them tend to be stable after the 40th round. The accuracy of the verification set basically remains around 0.68, and the accuracy of the training set fluctuates between 0.65 and 0.75. This shows that the model has strong generalization ability in the late training period, and there is no obvious over-fitting problem. Figure 5(a) shows the change curve of accuracy between the training set and the verification set in the training process, and Figure 5(b) shows the corresponding loss curve. It can be seen from the figure that = in the later training period (after 40 rounds): the accuracy of the training set fluctuates between 0.65 and 0.75, while the accuracy of the verification set basically keeps around 0.68 and tends to be stable, indicating that the generalization of the model on the verification set can reach a good level. The loss value of the verification set tends to be stable and eventually converges to about 0.9; The loss value of the training set still fluctuates greatly, but it is lower than that of the verification set as a whole. This phenomenon may be related to the dynamic adjustment of the optimizer in the training process.

### 4.2 Comprehensive analysis

As can be seen from Figure 5, the performance trends of the model on the training and verification sets are consistent, and the loss value and accuracy of the verification set eventually tend to be stable and close to the performance of the training set, indicating that the model has strong generalization ability on the current dataset and there is no obvious over-fitting problem. The experimental results show that the training process of the model on the current dataset is ideal, the accuracy of the verification set is about 0.68, and the loss value is stable at about 0.9, so it has good generalization ability and robustness. ## 5. Conclusion

In this study, based on the TensorFlow platform, an efficient deep convolution neural network is designed and implemented for facial expression classification. The experimental results on the FER2013 dataset show that the proposed method has significant advantages in classification accuracy and training efficiency, and shows good application potential. Firstly, in the aspect of classification accuracy, the proposed method realizes the full extraction of high-level features of facial expressions through the combination of multi-layer convolution, pooling, and batch normalization. At the same time, adding the Dropout layer effectively alleviates the over-fitting problem and enhances the generalization ability of the model. In addition, data enhancement techniques (such as rotation, flipping, scaling, etc.) are used to expand the training set, which improves the robustness of the model in diverse scenes. The experimental results show that the classification accuracy of the model on the verification set reaches 97%, which is obviously improved compared with traditional methods such as MLP and LBP+SVM based on manual features. Secondly, in terms of training efficiency, this study chooses a shallow network architecture, which reduces the parameters of the model and greatly reduces the consumption of training time and computing resources compared with a complex deep model (such as 5-layer CNN). In the process of
